key_terms: A query engine linked into an application process that provides analytical operators without a separate query server.
A narrow request interface, here an allowlisted region and a bounded row limit, that never accepts table names, paths or SQL text from callers.
An explicit set of permitted request values. Anything outside it is rejected before a query is planned or executed.
Independent bounds on input, computation and output. A SQL LIMIT bounds returned rows but not scanned input, join state, sort work or execution time.
The SHA256 of the canonical source rows reported with each result. It identifies which bytes produced the answer but does not prove authorization or scientific validity.

worked_examples.title: Validate a request before creating a session
worked_examples.output:
accepted {'region': 'east', 'limit': 2}
rejected Limit must be an integer from one to three
worked_examples.interpretation: The first request passes and the second fails even though True compares equal to 1 in Python, because the check uses an exact type test rather than isinstance. Rejecting before a session exists means a malformed request costs no engine memory and leaves no partial receipt. Keep the approved query text on the server keyed by region; never splice a caller string into SQL.

worked_examples.title: Fingerprint the source in each response
worked_examples.code:
import hashlib
import json

SOURCE = [{"id": 1, "region": "east", "amount": 4}, {"id": 3, "region": "east", "amount": 7}]
canonical = json.dumps(SOURCE, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
print(hashlib.sha256(canonical.encode()).hexdigest()[:16])
worked_examples.interpretation: The digest prefix is stable for this exact source and changes if any value, key or row changes, so two responses can be compared for source identity without shipping the data. Sorting keys and fixing separators matters: the default JSON separators or a different key order would produce a different hash for the same facts. Include the full digest in real responses; the prefix here only keeps the output short.

evidence: Complete actual local program with independent expected values and explicit negative checks; distributed-system claims are excluded.
